elements.element: Commitment to obtain the bundled Monthly Base Fee Services is limited to the current 12-month term (not the full multi-year Term)
elements.evidence: "through the end of the then-current twelve (12) month period only" (replacing "during the Term")

elements.element: Customer may reduce/discontinue the committed volume on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Customer may, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to M&I, discontinue or reduce any Service included in the Monthly Base Fee"

elements.element: Reduction results in a true-up (equitable adjustment) rather than a penalty or shortfall charge
elements.evidence: "the parties shall equitably reduce the Monthly Base Fee to reflect the resource units no longer used"; "No shortfall, penalty or similar charge shall be payable by Customer"

elements.element: No minimum commitment of any kind exists
elements.evidence: "a minimum monthly fee (\"Monthly Base Fee\") for certain bundled data processing Services" remains, and Customer "shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services"

elements.element: Fees are charged for usage or ordered services only
elements.evidence: "multiplied by the greater of (a) the Monthly Base Fee ... plus any other minimum monthly fee" — minimum-fee and Estimated Remaining Value constructs untouched

offending_extra_words: No shortfall, penalty or similar charge shall be payable by Customer in connection with any such discontinuation or reduction.
reasons: All three atomic fallback elements are satisfied on the operative text: the commitment is capped at the then-current twelve-month period, reduction is permitted on 30 days' notice, and the consequence is an equitable reduction of the Monthly Base Fee with no shortfall or penalty.

Preferred is not met and was not the locked target: the Monthly Base Fee minimum and the mandatory obligation to take the full bundle survive, as does the Estimated Remaining Value formula built on minimum monthly fees.

Minimality fails: the single replacement expands 32 words to 103 (ratio 3.22) with a 0.767 changed-character ratio, exceeding the official gates. The same result could be achieved by (i) replacing "during the Term" with "during the then-current twelve (12) month period" and (ii) adding one short sentence permitting reduction on 30 days' notice with an equitable fee adjustment, anchored against a larger unchanged span.

The final sentence largely duplicates the protection already delivered by "equitably reduce the Monthly Base Fee"; the belt-and-braces "or similar charge" wording and "prior written" formality are more than needed to complete the fallback.

Intent is preserved: Schedule 6.2, the resource-unit overage mechanic, and the surrounding definitions remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced ("then-current twelve (12) month period" is self-contained).
